entries.question_title: Buck-boost converter CCM peak-to-peak inductor current ripple
entries.key_topic: Inductor current ripple in inverting buck-boost converter operating in CCM
entries.asked_for: Peak-to-peak inductor current ripple ΔIL in amperes
entries.method_summary: Use buck-boost CCM duty D=|Vo|/(Vdc+|Vo|)=0.25, ton=D/fpwm=5 us, then ΔIL=(Vdc/L)ton=0.4545 A.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: buck-boost CCM switch-on inductor voltage vL=Vdc

entries.question_title: Closed-loop buck converter Vdc from C2 voltage and PWM control
entries.key_topic: Closed-loop buck converter steady-state control calculation
entries.caption: Closed-loop buck converter feedback-control case study: the circuit uses a PWM sawtooth comparator, compensator output, and feedback divider to determine the required input voltage Vdc when vC2 = 0.5 V, R12 = 4 kΩ, R13 = 3 kΩ, βVref = 2.5 V, and vsaw = 5 V.
entries.method_summary: Use α=R13/(R12+R13)=3/7, αVo=βVref=2.5 V, so Vo=5.833 V. With vC2=0.5 V, u=3.0 V, δ=u/vsaw=0.6, and Vo=δVdc, giving Vdc=9.72 V.
formula_source: Ideal buck converter relation: Vo = δVdc
Circuit reasoning: feedback divider α = R13/(R12+R13)

entries.question_title: Turn-off snubber resistor from minimum duty cycle
entries.key_topic: Sizing Rs so Cs discharges during MOSFET on-time
entries.caption: Turn-off snubber sizing case study for a MOSFET chopper with inductive-load current source: the circuit uses a snubber capacitor Cs, snubber diode Ds, and discharge resistor Rs to limit the MOSFET drain-source voltage rise at turn-off; here Vdc = 200 V, fpwm = 6 kHz, Cs = 58 nF, and the worst-case minimum duty cycle is 10%.
entries.method_summary: Worst-case discharge time is ton,min=0.10/6000=16.67 us. Using the ELE336 RC settling rule ton,min=3*2.2*Rs*Cs, Rs=16.67 us/(6.6*58 nF)=43.54 ohm.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: Cs discharges through Rs during MOSFET on-time
RC transient rule: settled after about 3 rise/fall intervals
10%-90% RC rise/fall-time approximation: tr ≈ 2.2 Rs Cs

entries.question_title: H-bridge average voltage from S1 duty cycle
entries.key_topic: Average output voltage of a bipolar H-bridge switching waveform
entries.caption: H-bridge converter average-load-voltage question: four MOSFETs and four antiparallel diodes form a full bridge connected to a 400 V DC link, with a resistive load of 127 Ω and switch S1 operated at 35% duty cycle.
entries.method_summary: For bipolar H-bridge average voltage, Vavg=Vdc(2d−1)=400(2*0.35−1)=-120 V.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: +Vdc for duty d and -Vdc for duty 1-d

entries.question_title: Forward converter volt-second balance equation for L
entries.key_topic: Selecting correct inductor volt-second balance equation for a forward converter in CCM
entries.caption: Forward converter CCM volt-second-balance question: during the switch-on interval the secondary applies approximately (N2/N1)Vdc to the output filter, so the inductor voltage is (N2/N1)Vdc − Vo; during the freewheel interval the inductor voltage is −Vo.
entries.asked_for: Correct volt-second balance equation for L
entries.method_summary: On-time vL=(N2/N1)Vdc−Vo; off-time vL=−Vo. Volt-second balance gives δ[(N2/N1)Vdc−Vo]+(1−δ)(−Vo)=0.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: transformer secondary voltage and freewheel interval

entries.question_title: Buck-boost converter volt-second balance equation for L
entries.key_topic: Selecting correct inductor volt-second balance equation for a buck-boost converter in CCM
entries.caption: Buck-boost converter CCM volt-second-balance question: during switch-on the inductor voltage is +Vdc, and during diode-conduction/switch-off the inductor voltage is Vo, where Vo is drawn with negative polarity for the inverting buck-boost output.
entries.asked_for: Correct volt-second balance equation for L
entries.method_summary: On-time vL=Vdc; off-time vL=Vo using signed output-voltage convention. Volt-second balance gives δVdc+(1−δ)Vo=0.
formula_source: Circuit reasoning: buck-boost inductor voltage in switch-on and diode-conduction intervals
